title: fix(components): action:bar / action:group / action:menu members evaluate properties.params like a top-level action:button (objectui#10290)
body:
Fixes #10290
Clause-②: no

## What changed

- `action:bar` evaluates an inline member's `properties` where it composes the member for `action:button` / `action:icon` (`withEvaluatedProperties` in `static-params.ts`). An overflow member goes to the bar's `action:menu` as authored, and that renderer evaluates it when it runs it, so no value is evaluated twice.
- `action:group` and `action:menu` read an item's `properties.params`, evaluated with the same evaluator (`readMemberStaticParamValues`), and forward it as `ActionDef.params`. An item that carries an `ActionParam[]` list forwards both channels, as `action:button` does. A node-level object `params` keeps its objectui#10462 handling: dropped with one development warning, and the `type: 'api'` window unchanged. `properties.params` wins over that window's object, as it wins over a node-level object on `action:button`.
- `@object-ui/react`: the memo's per-key rule, its scope builder and its `properties` loop move from the memo closure to module scope in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` (`evaluateConfigValueWith`, `configEvaluationScope`, `evaluateConfigBagWith`). The memo calls them; its behaviour is unchanged. New exports: `useConfigBagEvaluator()` (`hooks/useConfigBagEvaluator.ts`) and its plain half `evaluateConfigBagInScope()` (`SchemaRenderer.tsx`). **File-surface widening, declared:** the route needs these exports.
- Changeset `.changeset/10290-container-member-params-evaluated.md`: `@object-ui/components` patch, `@object-ui/react` patch.

## H1: premise, measured on base `17b323e5ca`

Instrument: a one-off probe (not committed) that printed each handler's `params`, then the committed pin file run at the base in a detached control worktree. The page is a record page bound through `RecordContextProvider` to `{ id: 'rec_1' }`. The member is authored `properties.params: { objectName: 'account', recordId: '${record.id}' }`, and the handler is `navigate_edit`.

| path | `params` the handler received | template evaluated |
|---|---|---|
| CONTROL: top-level `action:button` through `SchemaRenderer` | `{ objectName: 'account', recordId: 'rec_1' }` | yes |
| `action:bar` inline member | `{ objectName: 'account', recordId: '${record.id}' }` | no, raw |
| `action:bar` member, `component: 'action:group'` | same raw object | no, raw |
| `action:bar` member, `component: 'action:menu'` (overflow) | `undefined` | values dropped |
| `action:bar` member spilled past `maxVisible` | `undefined` | values dropped |
| `action:group`, inline display | `undefined` | values dropped |
| `action:group`, dropdown display | `undefined` | values dropped |
| `action:menu` | `undefined` | values dropped |

The `component: 'action:icon'` bar row was added to the pin after the probe. It is red on base in the pin run below.

So PR objectui#10460 evaluates on none of the three containers, and the premise holds. The overflow, group and menu paths did not read `properties.params` at all.

## H2: the evaluator and the route

- **The evaluator.** Inside `SchemaRenderer`'s `evaluatedSchema` memo, `evaluateConfigValue(key, value)` does the work. A `params` bag goes through `mapParamsLeaves` (`utils/paramsBag.ts`) with a visitor that calls `evaluator.evaluate` on each string leaf. Any other value goes through `ExpressionEvaluator.evaluate` per value, with a CEL envelope preserved and a data object passed through. `evaluator` is `new ExpressionEvaluator(scope)` from `@object-ui/core`. Its scope is the ambient predicate scope, plus `current_user` (an alias of `user`), plus `record` (the RecordContext row, only when one is bound), plus `page` (page variables). None of this was exported before this PR.
- **Route (a) taken:** each container calls that rule with that scope.
- **Route (b) not viable.** Dropdown items (the `action:group` dropdown, `action:menu`, and the bar overflow) are `DropdownMenuItem` leaves, not registry nodes, so `SchemaRenderer` cannot mount them. For inline members, (b) would also run the `properties` hoist on each member, a second run of the node visibility and enablement gate, and the `data-obj-*` and style plumbing. That is a wider behaviour change than the card asks for.
- **Scope each container has at hand.** Four sources: the host's `data` row prop (what the members' `visible` / `disabled` predicates bind as `record`), the RecordContext row, page variables and the ambient predicate scope. The last three are the contexts `SchemaRenderer` reads, and the containers render under the same providers. `useConfigBagEvaluator` reads exactly the memo's three inputs. So a member's templates bind the RecordContext row, as a top-level `action:button`'s do. The `data` prop is not bound into the template scope, and `SchemaRenderer` does not bind it either.
- **Why the hook lives in `hooks/` and not in `SchemaRenderer.tsx`.** Measured: a hook declared in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` puts that file under the React Compiler lint. The lint then reports three pre-existing render-time `performance.now()` / `Date.now()` debug probes as `react-hooks/purity` errors (0 without the hook, 3 with it).

## H3: `visible` / `disabled` on these paths

Measured on base with a one-off probe on the same 7 paths plus the control. The predicates were `record.id == 'rec_1'` (true on the page), `record.id == 'rec_2'` (false), `disabled: record.id == 'rec_1'`, and the template form `${record.id == 'rec_1'}`.

- **With the host's `data` row passed** (as `DetailView` passes `data={data}`): all 8 rows evaluate correctly. True renders, false is absent, disabled-true is disabled, and the template form renders. This is identical to the control. These gates are evaluated already, and nothing was widened.
- **Without a `data` row** (RecordContext only): `record` is unbound on the predicate tier, which binds `record` from the `data` prop through `usePredicateRecordContext`. The predicates fault: fail-closed (absent) on the `action:button` / `action:menu` leaves, fail-soft (shown) on the `action:group` leaves. The control top-level `action:button` does the same. This is not container-specific. It is recorded under Acceptance notes, with no card.

## Pins and ablation

New file `packages/components/src/renderers/action/__tests__/action-container-member-params-10290.test.tsx`, 17 tests:

- CONTROL: a top-level `action:button` through `SchemaRenderer` resolves `${record.id}`. Green on base and head.
- 8 paths × "the handler receives `properties.params` with `${record.id}` resolved". The paths are: bar inline, bar `action:icon`, bar group-placed, bar menu-placed, bar spilled past `maxVisible`, group inline, group dropdown, and menu.
- 8 paths × "a node-level `params` OBJECT is still not a values channel, and says so once" (ruling A).

Red on base, green on head:

- base `17b323e5ca` (control worktree, same test file): `Tests  8 failed | 9 passed (17)`. The 8 failures are exactly the 8 "resolved" rows. The control and the 8 node-level rows are green.
- head `e8b96c0161`: `Tests  17 passed (17)`.

Ablation: one leg, through objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, on the committed head. In `packages/react/src/hooks/useConfigBagEvaluator.ts`, the anchor `evaluateConfigBagInScope(bag, predicateScope, boundRecord, pageVariables);` became `bag; /* ABLATION-10290 */`, so the hook hands the bag back unevaluated.

- Predicted: the 8 resolved rows go red, and the control and node-level rows stay green.
- Observed: anchor 1 → 0, blob `8b01c529` → `f4c00a8f`, and `Tests  8 failed | 9 passed (17)`.
- Restore: blob == HEAD `8b01c529`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- No build leg: the suite resolves `@object-ui/react` through the root `vitest.config.mts` alias to `packages/react/src`, so the mutated source is what ran.

## Gates

At head `e8b96c0161` unless noted.

- **vitest union** (repo root): `packages/components/src/renderers/action/`, `packages/react/`, and the scripts tests for check-action-forward-parity (plus its closing-keyword test), check-doc-expression-carriage and check-component-surface-parity. Result: `Test Files  130 passed (130)`, `Tests  1883 passed (1883)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **`type-check`** (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) for `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/components`: Done / Done at `a60555f057`, after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react build`. The only later commit is changeset text.
  - The components test tsconfig includes the new pin file (`--listFilesOnly` count 1).
  - `dist/hooks/useConfigBagEvaluator.d.ts` is the only declaration of the hook in `dist`, so the green components type-check read the rebuilt `.d.ts`.
- **eslint** on the 8 changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files, with inline config on (as `eslint .` runs per package): 0 errors, 48 warnings.
  - Population: the root `eslint.config.js` has `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']`, and there is no package-level config in `packages/react` or `packages/components`.
  - File count: 8, from `--format json`.
  - No type-aware linting is configured (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
  - The same 5 pre-existing files at base: 0 errors, 49 warnings. `SchemaRenderer.tsx` has 2 fewer `no-explicit-any` and 1 more `react-refresh/only-export-components` (for the new plain export).
- **Green:**
  - `check:action-forward-parity`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:self-import`.
  - `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unused-deps`, `check:side-effects-array`, `check:component-surface-parity` (report-only).
  - `check:changeset-claims` (report-only). The four pending changesets it names for `SchemaRenderer.tsx` were read, and none is falsified.
  - `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs`.
- **NOT MEASURED:** `check:eager-closure`. Reason: exit 2, PREREQUISITE NOT MET. There is no `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, which needs a console build. Declared to CI.
- **CI's runs:** repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test`.

## Serial

- PR objectui#8941, head `bb7d5e71`, was fetched into a private ref. `git merge-tree --write-tree` of HEAD against it exits 0 with no conflicts. It touches `action-bar.tsx`, and the merge is clean.
- `origin/main` at `bf14b646` (5 commits past the base): merge-tree exits 0. None of those commits touch this PR's files, so there is no merge commit.

## Acceptance notes

- **Docs.** `content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md` teaches `properties.params` on a top-level `action:button` only. The same authoring now works on a container member. The guide was not edited, because it is outside this order's file surface. If it is extended, it needs one caveat: the development-build unevaluated-expression diagnostic runs in the `SchemaRenderer` memo, so an unresolvable template on a container member reaches the handler raw without that report. Carrier: none named.
- **Boundary.** `element:button`'s inline `action` and `page:header`'s actions still read no `properties.params`. They are objectui#10462 surfaces, not containers.
- **Boundary.** Take an `action:bar` member of `type: 'api'` with an object `params`. The overflow `action:menu` reads it (the objectstack#5777 window, entry semantics), and the inline path ignores it (`action:button` semantics). This dates from objectui#10460 and objectui#10462, and is not changed here.
- **Observation (H3).** The predicate tier binds `record` from the host's `data` prop, and the template tier binds it from RecordContext. On a host that provides RecordContext but no `data`, a `record.*` predicate faults while a `record.*` template resolves. This predates this PR and is identical on a top-level `action:button`. It was not measured on a real host page.
- The new `@object-ui/react` exports are declared `patch` in the changeset (fixed group).
